title: Onboard tuning advisor for multi-architecture kernel choices
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'Tuning Advisor' service that automates kernel candidate selection and compilation tuning recommendations during model onboarding. The advisor will produce a ranked scorecard of kernel variants (MHA/GQA/MoE-aware) and emit a publishable performance profile that can be pinned to model versions or used as a baseline for canary rollouts.
background: Onboarding new model families is becoming manual and time-consuming: SRE/infra engineers generate ad-hoc compile matrices, run long end-to-end tests, and hand-craft pin lists. For MoE and GQA variants the search space explodes due to sharding and grouped-attention kernels. We need an automated advisor that codifies heuristics and short simulations to reduce time-to-profile and lower onboarding-to-production latency.
solution_outline: 1) Create a fast offline profiler that runs representative microbenchmarks (KV cache sizes, prefix lengths, typical batch shapes) and a short synthetic token-stream to collect latency, memory, and stability metrics across kernel builds. 2) Implement a scoring function that weights latency, p95 stability, memory headroom, and CPU compile time to produce a ranked list of kernel candidates. 3) Emit a standard 'profile blob' with metadata, confidence, rollback hints and compatibility matrix that the publishing API can ingest. 4) Provide an SDK CLI for onboarding engineers to run the advisor locally and surface a recommended profile for review.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor runs end-to-end offline profiling for a new model in < 45 minutes on a 4-GPU dev pool
Produces at least 3 ranked kernel candidates with numeric score breakdown (latency, p95, memory, compile seconds)
Generated profile blob validates against the runtime's profile schema and can be pushed via /profiles/publish (staging)
Profile includes automatic rollback hints (fallback kernel id) and estimated token-cost delta vs current default
Runtime can consume advisor-generated profile in canary mode and report expected telemetry within one hour
implementation_steps: Design schema for advisor profile blob and add compatibility metadata fields (arch, sharding, sequence_range, batch_shapes)
Build microbenchmark harness for MHA, GQA, and MoE shapes and integrate with existing compile pipeline (use transient artifacts, avoid persistent image churn)
Implement scoring pipeline with configurable weight overrides and export of top-N candidates
Add CLI command `redwood-advisor run --model <name> --shards <n>` and a `--simulate` flag to replay synthetic workloads
Add unit/integration tests and a staging profile publishing flow that wires to the profile publish API and console UI
Document advisor UX and include guardrails for security reviewers (no secret exfiltration, limited network egress)
Ship initial MVP behind feature-flag and collect telemetry for 2 weeks before broader enablement
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal infra team only; advisor runs invoked by onboarding engineers (feature flag on)
Beta: allow select customer-facing model owners to opt into advisor-suggested profiles in staging
Canary: publish advisor profile to 5% traffic for a single tenant with automatic rollback configured
GA: enable advisor UI in Console profile management and expose CLI for self-serve onboarding
risks: False positives: advisor may prefer a kernel that regresses on real prompt distributions despite synthetic benchmarks
Compile artifacts could consume CI GPU quota if runs are not throttled
Profile publishing without adequate safety nets could impact production latency for customers
